text.p: - Presidential election in Chechnya, despite minor irregularities, seems to be the most democratic of all elections held in Russia over the last few years.
- Russian delegation at the Council of Europe meeting in Strasbourg has had problems deciding who will head it.
- French President Jacques Chirac's visit to Moscow to meet President Yeltsin will most probably be a complete media black-out.
- Aslan Maskhadov trounces rivals in the Chechen presidential race. His main rival Shamil Basayev says Maskhadov has to change his entourage if they are to work together.
- President Yeltsin's television appearance dispels rumours his state of health has worsened.
- A flu epidemic sweeping Russia has already taken 15 lives.

- Chechnya has been firmly split between different clans and newly elected President Aslan Maskhadov will have to lend an attentive ear to his election rival if he wants to keep the rebel republic under control.
- Chechnya has outplayed Russia politically and has effectively achieved independence from Moscow.
- Chechnya with a president is a new headache for politicians.
- Russia is ready to recognise any Chechen president but is glad that it is not Basayev.
